cases.headline: Access failures at Tory conference leave wheelchair-user suspended in mid-air for more than an hour
cases.candidate_summary: Disability News Service reports that a powered-wheelchair user was suspended on an unsafe platform lift for more than an hour at the Conservative conference in Birmingham's ICC.

verified_evidence.text: Clive Gilbert, a powered-wheelchair user, was suspended on an unsafe platform lift for more than an hour at Birmingham's ICC during the Conservative conference.

atomic_claims.claim: A powered-wheelchair user was suspended on an unsafe platform lift for more than an hour.
The incident occurred at the Conservative conference in Birmingham's ICC.

cases.headline: Access failures at Tory conference leave wheelchair-user suspended in mid-air for more than an hour
cases.candidate_summary: Disability News Service reports that a powered-wheelchair user was left suspended in mid-air for over an hour due to an unsafe platform lift. The incident occurred at the Conservative conference in Birmingham's ICC, where the room was inaccessible by eight steps and a faulty lift.

verified_evidence.text: Clive Gilbert, a powered-wheelchair user, was suspended on an unsafe platform lift for more than an hour at Birmingham's ICC during the Conservative conference.
The event room was beyond eight steps and reached through the platform lift; four other disabled attendees needed the lift.
Policy Connect had not been warned about the room's access challenges.

qualifications: The source calls the lift unsafe; it does not establish that the room was inaccessible by both the steps and a faulty lift.

atomic_claims.claim: A powered-wheelchair user was suspended on an unsafe platform lift for more than an hour.
The incident occurred at the Conservative conference in Birmingham's ICC.
The room was inaccessible by eight steps and a faulty lift.

cases.headline: ENIL brings a disability rights perspective to OSCE/ODIHR discussions on hate crime and intersectionality
cases.candidate_summary: European Network on Independent Living developed a disability rights perspective on hate crime and intersectionality. They proposed an Ask, Assess, Adapt approach for supporting hate-crime victims with disabilities.

verified_evidence.text: ENIL participated in an ODIHR side event during the Warsaw Human Dimension Conference.
ENIL's intervention argued that disability should be part of intersectional hate-crime analysis from the beginning.
ENIL proposed Ask, Assess, Adapt for professionals supporting hate-crime victims.

qualifications: The evidence establishes participation, contribution and a proposal; it does not say ENIL developed the disability-rights perspective itself.

atomic_claims.claim: ENIL developed a disability rights perspective on hate crime and intersectionality.
ENIL proposed an Ask, Assess, Adapt approach for supporting hate-crime victims with disabilities.

cases.headline: World’s on Fire: a defiant story of hope and community
cases.candidate_summary: Disability Arts Online reports on World’s on Fire, a stage production written and directed by disabled playwright Vici Wreford-Sinnott. The production features a wheelchair-using character who keeps disability and access on the group’s agenda.

verified_evidence.text: The review identifies World’s on Fire as a production written and directed by Vici Wreford-Sinnott.
The review describes Bec, played by Beth Samuels and using a wheelchair, reminding the group to retain disability and access in its plans.

qualifications: The traceable evidence supplied here does not state whether Vici Wreford-Sinnott is disabled.

atomic_claims.claim: World’s on Fire was written and directed by Vici Wreford-Sinnott.
Vici Wreford-Sinnott is a disabled playwright.
The production features a wheelchair-using character who keeps disability and access on the group’s agenda.
